summary: Glacier National Park two-story cab built 1934; Forest Lookouts says the park service burned it in April 1963. Other lists give 1963 as destroyed. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Burned by the National Park Service in April 1963 according to the Forest Lookouts page; other lists give 1963 as the year it was destroyed or gone

events.note: Panorama photos recorded on July 26, 1935; the page does not say where they were taken
Trail to the lookout washed out by heavy spring rains; a trail camp was being set up in September 1948 (page entry dated September 17, 1948) to rebuild the trail
Burned by the National Park Service in April 1963 because it was no longer of any use
Listed as gone by firelookout.com and as destroyed by the Huckleberry Hiker blog, both for 1963

evidence.supports: built 1934 as a two-story frame cab

evidence.quote: 1934: 2-story NPS cab at mid-slope hillside 1/2 mile north of summit. Gone 1963.

corrections.why: Both the firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts pages describe a two-story cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 48.93557, -113.75050, which lies north of Saint Mary while firelookout.com places the lookout about five miles south of Saint Mary. The stored coordinates (48.66771, -113.44546) match the firelookout.com description, so they are kept and the association's pair is treated as an error.

sources.title: The Huckleberry Hiker: The Fire Lookouts of Glacier National Park

notes_for_editor: Built 1934 and gone or destroyed 1963 agree across three sources. The burning by the National Park Service in April 1963 rests on the Forest Lookouts page alone. The Kemnow page's 1948 trail item quotes the Hungry Horse News. No NPS record, NRHP listing or historic structure report was found; the NRHP nomination fetched did not mention Curly Bear. The SummitPost listing from search snippets gives the same 1934 and 1963 dates but was not fetched, so it is not cited. Two WebSearch queries used. The brief's kind 'unknown' is corrected to two_story. Editor could check the NPS List of Classified Structures for an official removal record. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the September 17, 1948 entry and its Hungry Horse News attribution were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page; the story no longer repeats the association's coordinates, and the 1935 panorama note no longer says where the photos were taken.
